statement: A sequence starts at some rational number $x_1>1$, and is subsequently defined by $x_{n+1}=\dfrac{x_n\cdot n}{\lfloor x_n\cdot n\rfloor}$. Show that $k>0$ exists with $x_k=1$.

Triangle $\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in circle $\Omega$. Let $I$ be its incenter and $I_A$ its $A$-excenter. Let $N$ be the midpoint of arc $BAC$. Line $NI_A$ meets $\Omega$ again at $T$. The perpendicular to $AI$ at $I$ meets sides $AC$ and $AB$ at $E$ and $F$ respectively. The circumcircle of $\triangle BFT$ meets $BI_A$ again at $P$, and the circumcircle of $\triangle CET$ meets $CI_A$ again at $Q$. Prove that $PQ$ passes through the antipodal to $A$ on $\Omega$.
For a positive integer $n\geq 2$, does there exist positive integer solutions to the system $\begin{cases}a^n-2b^n=1,\\b^n-2c^n=1.\end{cases}$
A graph with $10^{100}$ vertices satisfies: every simple odd cycle has length $>100$. Prove there is an independent set of size at least $\dfrac{10^{100}}{102}$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcenter $O$. The internal angle bisectors of $\angle DAB$, $\angle ABC$, $\angle BCD$, $\angle CDA$ create a convex quadrilateral $Q_1$. The external bisectors of the same angles create another convex quadrilateral $Q_2$. Prove $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ are cyclic, and that $O$ is the midpoint of the segment connecting their circumcenters.

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of functions $\mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$. It is known that for all $f,g\in\mathcal{F}$ there exists $h\in\mathcal{F}$ such that for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^+$: $y^2\cdot f\!\left(\tfrac{g(x)}{y}\right)=h(xy)$. Prove that for all $f\in\mathcal{F}$ and all $x\in\mathbb{R}^+$: $f\!\left(\tfrac{x}{f(x)}\right)=1$.

Given cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, define $E=AD\cap BC$ and $F=AB\cap CD$. Let $\Omega_A$ be the circle through $A,D$ tangent to $AB$ with center $O_A$. Let $\Gamma_B$ be the circle through $B,C$ tangent to $AB$ with center $O_B$. Let $\Gamma_C$ be the circle through $B,C$ tangent to $CD$ with center $O_C$. Let $\Omega_D$ be the circle through $A,D$ tangent to $CD$ with center $O_D$. Prove that $O_AO_BO_CO_D$ is cyclic and its center lies on $EF$.
Let $n$ be a positive integer. A graph on $2n-1$ vertices is given such that the size of the largest clique is $n$. Prove that there exists a vertex that is present in every clique of size $n$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB=AC$. Let $D$ be a point on $AC$. Let $L$ be a point inside the triangle such that $\angle CLD=90^\circ$ and $CL\cdot BD=BL\cdot CD$. Prove that the circumcenter of triangle $\triangle BDL$ lies on line $AB$.

Let $G$ be a graph colored using $k$ colors. Say a vertex is forced if it has neighbors in all the other $k-1$ colors. Prove that for any 2024-regular graph $G$ with no triangles or quadrilaterals, there exists a coloring using 2025 colors such that at least 1013 of the colors have a forced vertex of that color.

Let $f(N)$ denote the maximum number of T-tetrominoes that can be placed on an $N\times N$ board such that each T-tetromino covers at least one cell not covered by any other T-tetromino. Find the smallest real $c$ such that $f(N)\leq cN^2$ for all positive integers $N$.

Prove that for all primes $p$ such that $p\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ or $p\equiv 5\pmod{8}$, there exist integers $1\leq a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_{(p-1)/2}<p$ such that $\displaystyle\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq(p-1)/2}(a_i+a_j)^2\equiv 1\pmod{p}$.
